what: What every land vehicle and gun could do, as measured: armour by facing, the gun by range, speed, ground pressure, rate of fire, reliability. Keyed by the names in index-land.json. Made by tools/battle-models/land/performance.py.
asked: Brian, 22 Nov 2026: the named tanks have real advantages from their measured performance against their peers; German tanks are far weaker at the back, so hits there pay; the shared vehicles vary a little by country.
sure: every vehicle and gun carries `sure`: high, medium or low (the standard published figures, set down by the modeller), or design (our own invention: no history to check).
checked: by the historian on 22 Nov 2026 (historian/land-performance-check-1122.md): the Tiger and Panther finding confirmed, and the corrections there are in this file. Not checked: the row Type97:47 and her gun (the modeller's own figures); the month taken for the M93 round (the check says late 1944); the hollow-charge dates, found on no page and marked low.

units.armour: mm, and slope in degrees from the vertical
units.pierce_30deg_mm: mm of rolled plate pierced at 30 degrees from square-on, at ranges_m, by each nation's own table (good to about one part in ten across nations)
units.soft_ground: 0 to 1: how well she keeps going in mud, snow and sand (ground pressure, track width, wheels)
units.radio: the share of her kind that can talk to each other
units.optics: 1.0 is a good plain sight; the German sights are the best
units.command: 1.0 is three men in the turret with a cupola; less where the commander must also lay or load
units.reliability: 0 to 1, a judgment: about the share still running after a long march
units.fire_when_pierced: a judgment from wartime surveys: how often she burns when a shot comes through that face; explodes_of_fires: how many of those end with her ammunition going up
units.worth_mm: each face as one number: the upright plate it is worth against a 75 mm shot
units.weaker_than_front: how many times weaker the side and the rear are than the front

rule.need: mm x quality / cos(slope)^(1+k), k = 0.5 x mm / calibre - 0.2 held in 0 .. 0.5
rule.chance: smooth step of (square / need): 0 at 0.85, half at 1.00, sure at 1.15
rule.face: the chances on its plates, each by its share
rule.hollow_charge: a gun with heat_mm pierces that much square-on at any range to heat_to_m, from the month heat_from; before it, use `before_hollow_charge` in duels and reach
rule.later_rounds: duels and reach are worked with each gun's first round. From a later round's month multiply that gun's piercing row by its `times` and judge again by this rule (scarce: a few rounds a gun; only: the nations that had it)
rule.then: a shot that comes through puts her out of the fight `kills_when_it_pierces` of the time (the shooter's), and she burns `fire_when_pierced` of the time by the face (the target's)

kwk37.name: 7.5 cm KwK 37 L/24
kwk37.note: a short support gun; hollow charge from 1942 (about 70 mm at first, 75 late in 1942, 100 in 1943: the dates are the weakest part)

lefh18.name: 10.5 cm leFH 18
lefh18.note: a howitzer: the armour-piercing table is the weakest figure here

sfh18.name: 15 cm sFH 18/1 L/30
sfh18.note: a heavy howitzer; her shell's burst breaks about 40 mm of plate

f34.name: 76.2 mm F-34 L/41.5 (and the KV's ZiS-5)
f34.note: Soviet tables count a pierce more strictly than German ones

m3_75.name: 75 mm M3 L/40
m3_75.note: the best high-explosive shell of any tank gun of its size

m7_76.name: 3-inch M7 L/50
m7_76.note: M93: 135 mm at 1,000 yards, from late 1944, a few rounds a gun

qf2.name: QF 2-pounder L/52
qf2.note: its high-explosive shell was not made until late 1942 and rarely issued: helpless against a dug-in gun. A capped shot came later (about 49 mm at 1,000 yards)

qf25.name: QF 25-pounder
qf25.shell: AP shot (609 m/s on the top charge)

qf6.name: QF 6-pounder L/50 (57 mm)
qf6.note: the sabot shot was scarce and less accurate

sa35_75.name: 75 mm SA 35 L/17 (in the hull)
sa35_75.note: laid by turning the whole tank

t97_57.name: 57 mm Type 97 L/18
t97_57.note: an infantry support gun: little use against a tank

t1_47.name: 47 mm Type 1 L/48
t1_47.note: Japan's one real tank-killing gun: through a Sherman's side at battle range, not her front

any37.name: 37 mm gun (our own light tank and armoured car)

any57.name: 57 mm anti-tank gun (the one every other army shares)
any57.note: as the American M1 and the British 6-pounder it stands for; the later rounds are theirs alone

any75w.name: 75 mm gun (what-if tank hunter and breakthrough tank)

flame.name: flame projector
flame.note: kills men and open-topped vehicles at close range; nothing to a closed tank's plate

side.plate: lower hull side, behind the wheels

Tiger.edge: 100 mm in front and a gun that kills any tank of 1943 at 1,500 m: from the front she is all but proof against the 75 and 76 mm guns she meets
Tiger.flaw: her turret takes a minute to turn all the way round with the engine idling (about 20 seconds with it revved), she is slow, thirsty and breaks down; her side and rear are 80 mm, a fifth thinner than her front, with the engine, the petrol and the ammunition bins behind them
Tiger.note: her turret is driven off the engine: 6 degrees a second in low gear, up to 19 in high at 2,000 rpm. 10 is a working value; her model file still says 6, to mend at her next export

Panther.stands_for: Panzerkampfwagen V Panther Ausf. A and G
Panther.edge: the best gun and the best frontal armour of any medium tank: her sloped glacis turns every Allied tank gun of 1943-44 but the biggest, and she is fast across soft ground
Panther.flaw: a glass back: 40 to 50 mm on her sides and rear, a third of what her front is worth, so almost any gun kills her from the flank; her final drives fail and her engine bay burns
Panther.note: the true weak-backed German tank: side and rear are worth about 50 mm against a front worth about 130. The plates are the Ausf. G's; the Ausf. A's upper hull side was 40 mm at 40 degrees, worth about the same

PanzerIV.edge: a long 75 mm that kills a T-34 or a Sherman from the front at 1,000 m, a three-man turret, good sights and a radio in every tank
PanzerIV.flaw: thin and upright everywhere but her hull front: 50 mm on the turret face, 30 mm on her sides and only 20 mm on her tail
PanzerIV.note: the skirts are thin spaced plate against anti-tank rifles and hollow charges: they do nothing to a tank gun's shot

PanzerIV:short.stands_for: Panzerkampfwagen IV Ausf. F1 (the short gun, to early 1942)
PanzerIV:short.edge: a fine high-explosive gun for breaking infantry and guns, the same three-man turret and radio
PanzerIV:short.flaw: her short gun cannot pierce a T-34 or a Matilda from the front at any range
PanzerIV:short.note: the same model with the gun swap `short`; with the 1942 long L/43 gun use this row's armour and gun kwk40_43

StuG3.edge: the Panzer IV's gun and 80 mm in front in a hull barely two metres high: hard to see, hard to hit, deadly from ambush
StuG3.flaw: no turret: her gun swings only 10 degrees each way, so a tank on her flank is on her blind side, and her sides are 30 mm

Hummel.edge: a 150 mm howitzer that keeps up with the tanks: a 43 kg shell out to 13 km
Hummel.flaw: an open box of 10 mm plate that stops rifle bullets and nothing more; only 18 shells aboard

Hanomag.edge: carries ten men under sloped plate that stops rifle fire and splinters, across ground a lorry cannot cross
Hanomag.flaw: open on top and proof against nothing bigger than a rifle bullet

SdKfz222.edge: fast, small and quiet with a 20 mm automatic gun: sees first and gets away
SdKfz222.flaw: wheels and 8 mm plate: off the road she bogs, and any tank gun ends her

FlakHalftrack.edge: 220 rounds a minute up to 2,000 m: death to a low aircraft, and to infantry and lorries on the ground
FlakHalftrack.flaw: no armour but the gun's shield

Pak40.edge: kills any Allied tank of 1942-44 from the front at 1,000 m, and stands barely waist-high in a hedge
Pak40.flaw: 1.4 tonnes: once in place she stays there, and her crew have only a shield

leFH18.edge: a 14.8 kg shell to 10.7 km, six a minute
leFH18.flaw: outranged by the Soviet and British guns of her class

T34.edge: sloped armour all round worth twice its thickness in front, wide tracks that float her over mud and snow, a diesel engine, and the fastest of the mediums
T34.flaw: her commander is also her gunner, so she spots and shoots slowly; poor sights, few radios before 1943, and her fuel tanks line the fighting compartment: pierced, she burns, and half-empty tanks blow up
T34.note: reliability is 0.65 for tanks built in 1942, 0.8 from mid-1943. Fire: a Soviet study of 72 wrecks from Kursk found 68 in 100 destroyed by the diesel in her fuel tanks burning, with the ammunition mostly whole in its racks: diesel did not save her

T34-85.edge: an 85 mm gun that pierces a Tiger's side at 1,000 m and a Panther's side at any range, a three-man turret at last, and the T-34's speed and wide tracks
T34-85.flaw: her hull is still the 45 mm of 1940: the long German 75 and the 88 go through her front at any battle range, and her fuel tanks still line the fighting compartment, so pierced she burns

KV1.edge: 75 mm or more on every face: in 1941 no German tank gun can pierce her from any side, only the 88 mm flak gun
KV1.flaw: the same gun as the far cheaper T-34, a clutch and gearbox that fail on the march, too heavy for most bridges, and slow

SU85.edge: the 85 mm gun on the T-34's hull months before the T-34-85: kills a Tiger from the side at 1,000 m
SU85.flaw: no turret (10 degrees each way) and no machine gun: helpless against infantry close in

SU76.edge: the ZiS-3 field gun on light tracks that go where the infantry go, through marsh and snow
SU76.flaw: open on top and at the back, 10 to 35 mm of plate, two petrol engines beside the driver

ZiS3.edge: field gun and anti-tank gun in one: 15 rounds a minute, 13 km of range, light enough for its crew to push
ZiS3.flaw: against a Tiger or a Panther's front it is useless beyond point-blank

Sherman.stands_for: Medium Tank M4 and M4A1, 75 mm
Sherman.edge: the most reliable tank of the war, a fast power-traversed turret that gets the first shot off, a gun steadied for firing on the move, the best high-explosive shell, and a radio in every tank
Sherman.flaw: her 75 mm cannot pierce a Tiger or a Panther from the front at any range; tall, narrow-tracked, and until wet stowage (1944) four in five burn when pierced through the side
Sherman.note: 0.60 to 0.80 is the record for the early, dry-stowed tanks, and the culprit was mostly her ammunition, not her petrol; with wet ammunition stowage (1944 on) fire_when_pierced drops to about 0.15

M10.edge: a 3-inch gun that pierces a Tiger's side at 1,500 m and a Panzer IV from the front at any range, on the Sherman's reliable gear
M10.flaw: her turret is cranked round by hand, 80 seconds for a full turn, it is open to the sky, and her plate is 19 to 38 mm
M10.note: the model file says 12 degrees a second for her turret: history says about 4.5 (hand crank). To mend at her next export.

M7.edge: a 105 mm howitzer on the Sherman's hull: a 15 kg shell to 11 km wherever the tanks go

M3Halftrack.edge: fast, tough and never short of spares, with a heavy machine gun over the cab
M3Halftrack.flaw: 6 mm of upright plate: a rifle bullet at close range goes through

M16.edge: four heavy machine guns in a powered mount: 1,800 rounds a minute, turning 60 degrees a second

M8.edge: 89 km/h on a road, 560 km on a tank of fuel, and a 37 mm gun that kills any other armoured car
M8.flaw: thin floor and plate, wheels that bog in mud

Howitzer105.edge: accurate and tireless, and tied to the fastest fire-direction system of the war: many batteries on one target within minutes
Howitzer105.flaw: 11 km of range, less than the British and Soviet guns

Matilda.edge: 70 to 78 mm on every face: in 1940-41 no tank gun and no ordinary anti-tank gun can pierce her from any side
Matilda.flaw: 24 km/h at best, a small gun with no high-explosive shell at all, and a turret too small to take a bigger one
Matilda.note: her turret is turned by hydraulic power, by hand in an emergency; no page gives its speed, so 14 degrees a second is the modeller's figure (about 26 seconds a full turn)

Sexton.edge: the 25-pounder on a tank's hull, with 105 rounds aboard

25pdr.edge: turns all the way round on its firing platform in seconds, 12 km of range, and a solid shot that stops a 1941 tank
25pdr.flaw: a lighter shell (11.3 kg) than the 105 mm howitzers

CharB1.edge: 50 to 60 mm on every face in 1940, when German tank guns pierce 30 to 40: one held a village street against a whole column
CharB1.flaw: her commander is alone in the turret and must command, load, lay and fire; the 75 mm in the hull is aimed by turning the tank; six hours of fuel, and a radiator grille on her left side that a small gun can pierce

Gun75.edge: 15 aimed rounds a minute and more in a hurry: the fastest-firing field gun of its day
Gun75.flaw: a design of 1897: 6 degrees of swing without shifting the trail, and 8.5 km of range

M13.edge: a sound 47 mm gun, as good as the British 2-pounder and with a high-explosive shell besides
M13.flaw: riveted plate that cracks and throws its rivets when hit, an engine too weak for the desert, and a two-man turret

Semovente.edge: low, with 50 mm in front and a 75 mm whose hollow-charge shell pierces a Grant or a Sherman's side: Italy's best armoured vehicle in the desert
Semovente.flaw: a crew of three, a slow shell, and the same weak engine as the M13

L3.edge: tiny, cheap and quick: 1.3 m high
L3.flaw: two machine guns and plate a heavy machine gun pierces: no match for any real tank

Type97.edge: a reliable air-cooled diesel and light weight that crosses jungle tracks and weak bridges no Western medium can
Type97.flaw: 25 mm of plate and a short 57 mm made for shelling infantry: against a Sherman she can do nothing from any side but point-blank at the rear

Type97:47.stands_for: Type 97 Shinhoto Chi-Ha (the new turret and 47 mm gun, from 1942)
Type97:47.edge: the same light, reliable tank with a long 47 mm that goes through a Sherman's side and rear at battle range
Type97:47.flaw: still 25 mm of plate: any tank gun or anti-tank gun goes through her from any side
Type97:47.note: no model of her own yet: draw the Type97 model. A row so that Japan's tanks of 1942-45 are not left with the 57 mm; the historian asked for it and has not checked these figures

7TP.edge: the best gun of any light tank in 1939, a diesel engine and a good periscope: better than the Panzer I and II she meets
7TP.flaw: 17 mm of plate, and there were only about 130 of her

LightTank.stands_for: our own light tank of 1936-42 (in the manner of the Vickers and Czech export tanks)
LightTank.edge: cheap, light enough for any bridge, and a match for other light tanks
LightTank.flaw: 25 mm of riveted plate and a 37 mm gun: outclassed by every medium tank

MediumTank.stands_for: our own medium tank of 1940-45 (welded, sloped front, 50 mm gun)
MediumTank.edge: a sound three-man turret and 50 mm of sloped plate in front: equal to a 1941 medium
MediumTank.flaw: her 50 mm gun cannot pierce a T-34, a Sherman or a late Panzer IV from the front

AssaultGun.stands_for: our own assault gun (the medium tank's hull, a 75 mm in a fixed box)
AssaultGun.edge: a real 75 mm gun and 60 mm in front for the price of a medium tank

SelfPropelledGun.stands_for: our own self-propelled gun (the medium tank's hull, a 75 mm field gun in an open box)
SelfPropelledGun.edge: a field gun that keeps up with the tanks
SelfPropelledGun.flaw: an open box of 10 mm plate

ArmouredCar.stands_for: our own armoured car of 1936-45 (37 mm gun in a closed turret)
ArmouredCar.edge: fast on a road with a gun that kills other scouts
ArmouredCar.flaw: wheels, and plate against bullets only

AntiTankGun.stands_for: 57 mm anti-tank gun (as the American M1 and the British 6-pounder)
AntiTankGun.edge: kills a Panzer IV from the front at 1,000 m and a Tiger or a Panther through the side, and two men can swing it
AntiTankGun.flaw: nothing to a Tiger's or a Panther's front

Truck.edge: carries a section or tows a gun at 65 km/h on a road
Truck.flaw: no armour, and off the road in mud it stops

FlakTruck.stands_for: our own lorry with a 20 mm automatic gun
FlakTruck.edge: light flak that travels with the column

WhatIf_BreakthroughTank.edge: armour to walk through a gun line
WhatIf_BreakthroughTank.flaw: slow, costly, thin at the back

WhatIf_FlameTank.edge: burns infantry out of bunkers and houses
WhatIf_FlameTank.flaw: must close to 100 m, and burns fiercely herself

WhatIf_AmphibiousTank.edge: swims a river or comes ashore from a ship at 10 km/h

WhatIf_SnowTank.edge: very wide tracks: keeps going in deep snow and marsh that stops everything else
WhatIf_SnowTank.flaw: a light gun and light plate

WhatIf_GliderTank.edge: light enough to land by glider behind the enemy's line

duels.what: duels[shooter][target][face] = the chance a hit on that face comes through, at ranges_m

reach.what: reach[shooter][target][face] = the farthest range in metres at which a hit comes through one time in two (0: never; 2500: beyond the table)

shared_by_nation.what: the vehicles every small nation shares, a little different from country to country: multiply the shared design's armour (mm), gun (piercing), speed and reliability by these; `as` replaces the design's own numbers for a great power's real light tank; `later`: from that date the lean changes to the numbers given; `use_row`: from that date she has that tank itself, so take the named row of `vehicles` and no lean (LightTank@USA: the `as` row of USA here)

UK.after: Light Tank Mk VI: machine guns only

SWE.after: Stridsvagn m/38 to m/41, Bofors 37 mm

FIN.after: Vickers 6-ton and captured T-26, 45 mm gun

GRE.after: a handful of Vickers and captured Italian tankettes

MEX.after: Light Tank M3 and M5 by lend-lease

use_row.after: Light Tank M3 and M5 by lend-lease: whether any came during the war is not sure

BRA.after: Light Tank M3 by lend-lease, 1942 on

AFG.after: a few Italian and Soviet light tanks

FIN.after: captured T-28 and T-34, a handful

BRA.after: M3 Lee and M4 by lend-lease

use_row.after: StuG III Ausf. G bought in 1943

ROM.after: TACAM tank destroyers on captured hulls

use_row.after: StuG III Ausf. G supplied in 1943

MGL.after: Soviet BA-6 and BA-10, 45 mm gun

gaps: No model carries the British 17-pounder, the American 76 mm tank gun or 90 mm, the Soviet 122 mm or the German 88 mm L/71: the heaviest Allied gun here is the M10's 3-inch and the T-34-85's 85 mm.

The M10's turret speed in her model file (12 degrees a second) is faster than history (4.5, by hand: the historian confirms it), and the Tiger's file says 6 where this sheet says 10: both to mend at their next export. Until then take turret_degrees_a_second from here.
The Type 97 with the 47 mm gun (row Type97:47) has no model of her own and her figures are unchecked.
The what-if classes' figures are stand-ins by their size and role: the class table (sandbox arms) should overrule them.
